rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. I judged this from the supplied test source only and requested no implementation source.

**Resolution from the root against the retained outline, returning an owned `OutlineContent`**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. For each, it checks that `text()` equals the source span and that `structural_hash()` matches the item's.
- It also checks `ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())`, so selection reuses the retained outline.
- `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` covers percent-encoded names, `#N` duplicates, anonymous `section@` and `block@` selectors, and selecting from an already selected handle.
- `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` covers `#N` selection within nested parents.
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` selects `line@` items and checks their text.
- The empty selector returns the root, in `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` and `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors`.

**Shared source snapshot, no additional read, usable after the original handle is dropped**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` calls `drop(file)` and then rewrites the file on disk.
- After that, `selected_again` (selected from `file`) still reports "second", and the fingerprint is unchanged.
- `selected.select("")` still returns the original full text, so no re-read happened.
- A fresh `from_id` fails after the edit, which confirms the file really changed.

**Shared fingerprinting rules**
- `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` checks that a selected item keeps the language and scheme.
- A `custom-v3` language yields the same structural hash but a different fingerprint, so the scheme is carried into the selection.
- `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` checks that `text()` keeps the raw text while `format()` redacts it.

**Attached source in `text()`**
- The Rust test checks that the selected function's text starts with the doc comment and contains `#[inline]`. It also checks that the span covers the attached source.

**Selector syntax rules, including identical plain-text lines**
- `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` shows that identical `line` items select successfully and return "same".
- In the same test, duplicate non-line `part[same]` items return an ambiguity error.
- A `line` kind with differing hashes also returns an ambiguity error.
- `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` checks that the selector hash is twelve hex digits matching `structural_hash[..12]`, and that identical lines share a selector.

**Errors for invalid, missing, or ambiguous selections**
- `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` covers the malformed `fn[` and the missing `fn[absent]`.
- The ambiguity test covers ambiguous selections.
- The CSS test asserts that the un-numbered `rule[a%20b]` selector is an error.

**Gaps**
- I found no unmet obligation, and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.
- I did not treat out-of-range `#N` values as a gap. The requirement names no separate behavior for them, and the missing-item case is already covered.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineData;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
